objective: Recover a trustworthy model of an unfamiliar or messy repository, then make one evidence-backed improvement without broad speculative cleanup.

stages.purpose: Preserve current state and inventory instructions, manifests, modules, tests, CI, deployment, recent history, and the declared authority/freshness of material source documents.
stages.exit_when: The current technical surface, candidate sources of truth, and material source authority/freshness are known.

stages.purpose: Separate intended product behavior from accidental/stale implementation, reconcile current/draft/historical/unknown evidence without erasing conflicts, and identify the highest-leverage blocker.
evidence: explicit unresolved conflicts when no justified winner exists
stages.exit_when: A concise current-state model and prioritized recovery target are defensible from evidence, with conflicts and uncertainty preserved rather than silently resolved.

stages.purpose: Fix or stabilize one high-value current path before broad refactoring, using the reconstructed current baseline rather than stale artifacts as the implementation authority.
evidence: evidence that the chosen path follows the current source of truth
stages.exit_when: One meaningful path is more trustworthy and the next recovery priority is clearer.

pressure_guards.rule: Do not equate newest file, merged branch, or most detailed document with current truth. Track material source role/authority and freshness; Draft/Proposed/Historical evidence remains non-authoritative unless the project explicitly says otherwise.
When material sources disagree and authority/freshness do not justify a winner, preserve the conflict and uncertainty instead of silently selecting or rewriting history.

escalations.when: The project needs durable reconstruction of intent/specifications before continued feature work.
escalations.selection_rule: Prefer core Spec Kit existing-project/evolving-spec workflows first; treat community brownfield extensions as untrusted candidates until source and permissions are reviewed.

escalations.when: The repository is too large or long-running for the current host to maintain reliable context and isolated subproblems.
escalations.selection_rule: Select the runtime property actually missing; do not migrate merely because the repository is messy.

escalations.when: Recovery reveals that the immediate blocker is a bounded reproducible defect.
escalations.selection_rule: Reroute to bug-fix first; use mini-SWE-agent only if the issue is clear and verifiable.

verification: current-state claims are grounded in repository/runtime evidence
material sources have authority/freshness considered rather than being flattened into one truth
broad cleanup was avoided unless evidence justified it
reroute_signals: a specific failing behavior becomes primary -> bug-fix
a desired new behavior becomes primary -> feature-change
the user only needs a decision/review -> understand-review
